answer: Random audits plus decaying reputation stop cheap sybils. Each epoch a random sample of agents faces a pigment audit: they must reproduce recent work or lose their standing. Reputation also decays, so an identity cannot rest on one good week; it needs a steady nadir of fresh, verified contributions. A sybil farmer running many identities must keep all of them active and honest at once, and a single failed audit triggers a timber that freezes the whole cluster pending review. The cost of maintaining fakes rises with every epoch.
